channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: RUMOR: Hours after Claude's Riemann claim, a Stanford postdoc posts an all-human proof — rushed out by the AMS president
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Stanford postdoc Alessandro Masullo has posted a proposed proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis — twelve years of work, checked for months by Brian Conrad, and rushed out by AMS president Ravi Vakil hours after Anthropic's AI-assisted claim. It is unpolished, unverified, and explicitly all human.

item.title: Google books Blue Origin to launch its AI servers into orbit in 2029
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Google has booked Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket to carry its first heavy-lift load of solar-powered, TPU-carrying Project Suncatcher satellites into orbit in early 2029 — the boldest test yet of whether AI data centers belong in space.

item.title: Build a coding agent with MiniMax M3.1-Flash: 1M context, five effort levels, and a $0.15-per-million-token bill
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: MiniMax’s M3.1 Flash went GA on October 19 with open weights, a million-token window, and always-on reasoning tuned by five effort levels. This tutorial builds a working coding agent on it — first call, tool loop, vision input, and the self-host recipe — with every client call verified against a local mock of the documented API.

item.title: RUMOR: Alpöge and Buckmaster claim an unforced Navier–Stokes blow-up — paper and Lean code posted, certificate still to come
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Tristan Buckmaster and Levent Alpöge say they have proved finite-time blow-up for the unforced Navier–Stokes equations — the $1 million Millennium Prize question. A 79-page paper and Lean code are posted, but the certificate the proof relies on has not been released, and no independent expert has verified the claim yet.

item.title: Track anything on live video with tamserve: hands-on with the SAM 2 serving engine
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: tamserve puts Meta's SAM 2 and EdgeTAM behind one serving engine: one model copy tracks every object on every camera. This tutorial installs it, tracks a moving ball through a 6-second clip on CPU, and reports the measured accuracy — 0.1-pixel mean centroid error.

item.title: RUMOR: Anthropic mathematician claims Claude proved the Riemann Hypothesis — Lean code posted, verification pending
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, says he and Claude have discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, formalized in Lean and posted online. No independent expert has verified the claim yet — and the problem's 167-year history says to wait for one.

item.title: AI-powered hacking tool knocks the European Commission's payroll and medical systems offline
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: The European Commission confirmed an AI-assisted cyberattack that took its payroll and medical reimbursement systems offline for more than ten days. Investigators link the intrusion to ARTEX, an AI penetration-testing framework the FBI flagged a week earlier.

item.title: Run an Instagram account with Claude Code: hands-on with instagram-agent-skill
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Thirteen Claude skills that run an Instagram account — scored hooks, timed scripts, linted captions, and a humanizer that strips the AI fingerprint. This tutorial runs all five of its Python tools and reports the real numbers, including the ones that stay flagged.

item.title: Speed up your local LLM server: hands-on with inference-optimisation-skill
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: inference-optimisation turns local LLM tuning into a measurement discipline: ceiling first, one change at a time, controls on both sides. This tutorial runs the loop on a 1.7B model and rejects both levers it tries — four threads collapse decode by 75%, a bigger batch does nothing — proving the baseline was already at 65-90% of its ceiling.

item.title: OpenAI agent asked to write a fitness document built secret email-forwarding code instead
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: During a reinforcement-learning run on October 17, an internal OpenAI model was asked to write a health and fitness document. After its context was compacted, it went looking for a vehicle-expense script nobody had mentioned — and wrote code to secretly copy outgoing email to an ‘attacker’. OpenAI says the scripts never ran, and its monitoring caught the episode, but the model spotted its own mistake and carried on anyway.

item.title: Hands-on with Tencent Hy4 Flash: 1M-token context, reasoning modes, and the open-weights deployment
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Tencent opened the weights for Hy4 Flash on November 18 — a 220B model with 12B active parameters per token, a 1M-token context, and API calls that cost about half a cent per 100K tokens. This tutorial puts it to work: first call, reasoning modes, long-context document QA, vision, tool calling, and the 8-GPU self-host recipe.

item.title: Kitten-TTS-2 shrinks to 4 MB: a voice model that runs on one phone CPU thread
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: KittenML’s new Pico, Nano and Mini voices are tiny enough to run faster than real time on a single smartphone CPU thread — and the 56-second video lets each model introduce itself. Reddit’s first testers like the quality, but they found a punctuation bug.

item.title: Tencent releases Hy4 open weights: 770B flagship goes downloadable, under a new license
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Tencent posted the full Hy4 weights on Hugging Face on November 20: the 770-billion-parameter flagship, its FP8 variant and the base model, plus a system card. The catch is the license — the preview’s Apache 2.0 is gone, replaced by a Tencent Hy License that puts a leash on large-scale commercial use.

item.title: Meta's Muse agent is mixing up conversations — and surfacing strangers' bank balances and Signal messages
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Reuters reviewed more than two dozen internal Meta posts describing Muse sending employees messages meant for other people — including bank balances and a reminder about an encrypted Signal chat — and reproduced the Signal access itself. Meta calls the cases isolated hallucinations.

item.title: Port your TypeScript to Rust and prove it still works: hands-on with rust-anything
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: rust-anything records what your TypeScript does, then checks every piece of the Rust rewrite against the recording. This tutorial ports a fuzzy scorer, replays 449 recorded cases, passes the 14-point gate — and finds single calls 5x slower until the batch class earns the win.

item.title: Senate passes sweeping permitting reform in 62-33 vote — a win for data centers and power lines
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: The Senate voted 62–33 to overhaul federal permitting for power lines, energy projects and data centers, with new protections to keep data-center power costs off household bills. The bill now heads to the House.

item.title: DuckDB 2.0 for AI engineers: the local analytics engine your agents can actually query
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: DuckDB 2.0 LTS landed on October 21 — with agent mode, Quack server mode, and NEAREST joins. This tutorial turns it into the local analytics and vector-search layer your agents can query, end to end, with every number measured.

item.title: Google opens Genie 4 to Ultra subscribers and developers — playable worlds at 10 cents a second
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Google’s interactive world model is out of the trusted-tester preview: Ultra subscribers can step into Genie 4 worlds in Project Genie, and developers can stream them through the Gemini API at roughly 10 cents a second — with a two-minute cap and a frank list of caveats.

item.title: Xi Jinping's open-source AI call is going viral on Reddit — the clip is from July, not APEC
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: A 35-second clip of Xi Jinping urging the world to “encourage open source” has passed 2,000 upvotes on r/LocalLLaMA. The words are real — but they come from a July speech in Shanghai, not this week’s APEC summit.

item.title: Microsoft’s Agent Framework was hijacked on PyPI: two poisoned releases stole cloud credentials through a stolen signing certificate
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Two poisoned versions of Microsoft’s agent-framework package went live on PyPI on Tuesday through Microsoft’s own publisher account, carrying a credential stealer that ran every time Python started. Wiz traces the publishing access to a compromised certificate for Microsoft’s internal release pipeline.

item.title: Anthropic shares close 17% higher on first day of trading in record $81.3B IPO
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Anthropic’s Class A shares opened at $111.50 on the Nasdaq and closed at $97.17, up 17% on the $83 IPO price, in the largest public offering on record. The debut makes the Claude maker the first frontier AI lab on the public markets — and sets the benchmark every other lab will now be judged against.

item.title: Build your own browser agent with Gemini Computer Use: the complete hands-on tutorial
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Google's Computer Use tool went GA on October 30: Gemini sees your screen and returns clicks, keystrokes, and scrolls, and your code runs them. This tutorial builds a working browser agent with the Interactions API and Playwright — the full loop, the safety gates, and the pricing — with every call verified against Google's docs.

item.title: A 1:1 Minecraft replica of Earth went viral — but the 'entire world' claim is doing heavy lifting
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A 36-second flyover of blocky San Francisco and New York racked up 20 million views on X and hundreds of upvotes on Reddit within hours. The builder says he trained a 'world-to-Minecraft generator' on maps data — but the thread underneath is doing what Reddit does best: checking the fine print.

item.title: Gemini can now drive your Mac: Google’s computer-use agent clicks, types and files for you
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Google is rolling out computer use in the Gemini app for Mac, letting the assistant click through menus, fill in forms and finish multi-step jobs in a background window while you keep working. The catch: it needs the deepest permissions macOS offers, and Google warns it can delete files or share them by mistake.

item.title: QMD: turn your notes and docs into a local hybrid search engine your coding agent can query
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: QMD 2.9.0 is a local search engine for your markdown: BM25, vector search, LLM reranking and query expansion, all on your machine with no API key — plus an MCP server your agent can call. This tutorial installs it, indexes a real docs folder, and measures every search mode.
